observed.title: Route every list/table view through UnifiedTable to inherit the cold-load contract
observed.statement: Do not hand-roll a table (rows, loading skeleton, empty state, entrance animation). Use the shared UnifiedTable and pass `columns` + `data` + `isLoading`; it renders a permanent column header, a geometry-matched delayed ghost while loading-into-empty, a settled-only empty state, and an id-guarded row-entrance cascade that is COUPLED to `isLoading` — so the whole loading-pattern-v2 doctrine comes from two props with no per-page skeleton.
observed.detail_md:
## Problem

List views repeatedly re-implemented four things badly: a loading skeleton, an empty state, a ghost→content swap, and a row entrance animation. The failure mode is a blank/spinner flash on cold load and a big-bang reveal, plus `animate-pulse` skeletons that blink. A parallel fleet migrating plugin pages kept hitting Unified-backed tables that showed the ghost but then big-banged their rows, and skipped the cascade because it was a separate opt-in prop.

## The practice

`UnifiedTable` (`src/features/shared/components/display/UnifiedTable.tsx`) is the single table primitive. It encodes the five loading laws as a strict three-state body under a permanent header:

- `isLoading && data.length === 0` → calm, geometry-matched delayed ghost rows (`TableGhostRows`, `UnifiedTable.tsx:270`; ≥120ms `animate-fade-in`, fill-mode both, no `animate-pulse`). A fast fetch never paints one; a refetch WITH rows on screen never reaches this branch, so rendered data is never hidden (law 1). Body: `UnifiedTable.tsx:593`.
- `!isLoading && data.length === 0` → the settled empty state only (never flashes before the first fetch resolves — law 2).
- `data.length > 0` → rows that ripple in once via `useRowRevealEntrance` (`UnifiedTable.tsx:221`): id-guarded (`hasEntered(id)`), first-viewport only (`index >= REVEAL_CASCADE_ROWS` renders plain), capped 35ms stagger, reduced-motion aware — one-shot so poll/scroll/refetch never replay (law 4).

## What makes it a contract, not a helper

The row cascade is **coupled to the load** so callers get everything from `isLoading` alone. `resolveRowReveal(rowReveal, isLoading)` (`UnifiedTable.tsx:248`, applied at `:463`) enables the id-guarded cascade automatically whenever `isLoading` is passed; `rowReveal={true}` forces it on for store-backed data with no `isLoading`, `rowReveal={false}` opts out, `{resetKey}` re-ripples the same ids on a context switch. The id-guard makes auto-mode safe with no resetKey: same ids (refetch) never replay, new ids (filter change) ripple alone.

## What a session does differently

Stop writing a `<Skeleton/>`, a spinner branch, or a framer stagger for any table. Define `columns`, pass `data` + `isLoading`, done — you get ghost-under-chrome, empty-flash safety, and the rippling reveal for free. The header-doc contract at `UnifiedTable.tsx:1` states the rule for callers.

observed.title: Compose cold-load UX from four shared mechanics, never a per-page skeleton
observed.statement: For any async surface, do not build a bespoke skeleton or spinner. Compose four shared mechanics: (1) a delayed header-only RouteChunkSkeleton as the lazy-route Suspense fallback (kills the blank chunk-load gap, invisible when the chunk is warm); (2) ghost-under-permanent-chrome gated `isLoading && items.length === 0` so a fetch never hides rendered data; (3) an id-guarded RevealItem/useRevealTracker entrance cascade (one-shot, first-viewport, reduced-motion aware); (4) a module-scoped warm cache so a remount paints last-known data instead of re-ghosting. This is the full doctrine that the single existing 'delay lives on the placeholder' item is only law 3 of.
observed.detail_md:
## Delta vs the existing library item

The library already holds **"Put the loading delay on the placeholder, never on the content"** — that is law 3 (the CSS `animation-delay` is the anti-flash) and it stands. This item EXTENDS it with the concrete, reusable mechanics that implement the whole five-law doctrine (`docs/design/overview-loading.md`), which law 3 alone does not give you: the chunk-fallback, the three-state body, the row cascade, and warm-cache-on-remount.

## The four mechanics (all shared, all in-repo)

1. **Delayed route/chunk fallback** — `RouteChunkSkeleton` (`src/features/shared/components/layout/RouteChunkSkeleton.tsx:31`): a header-only ghost behind a 150ms `animate-fade-in` + `animationDelay` with fill-mode both (`:39-40`), used as the `Suspense` fallback for a lazy route so a cold first-open shows calm chrome, not a blank gap — and nothing at all once the chunk is warm/prefetched. Wired as the plugin/section fallback in `PersonasPage.tsx` (e.g. `:291`, `:300`), replacing `fallback={null}` and the centered-spinner `SuspenseFallback` (a law-5 violation).

2. **Ghost-under-permanent-chrome, gated on emptiness** — static chrome (header, tab strip, filter bar) always renders OUTSIDE the loading branch; the ghost renders under it only when `isLoading && items.length === 0`. A refetch with rows on screen never ghosts. Reference: `UnifiedTable.tsx:593` and `src/features/overview/sub_activity/components/GlobalExecutionList.tsx`.

3. **Id-guarded entrance cascade** — `RevealItem` (`src/features/shared/components/display/RevealItem.tsx`) is polymorphic (`as='div'|'tr'|'li'`, `:34`) so it wraps table/list rows directly (a `<div>` is invalid inside `<tbody>`/`<ul>`); it marks entry on `animationend` (`:76`) and honors reduced motion (`:57`). Paired with `useRevealTracker(resetKey)` the entered-id set survives virtual remount, so scroll/poll/refetch never replay.

4. **Warm-cache-on-remount** — a lazy route fully unmounts on nav-away, so data kept in component `useState` is lost and the surface cold-flashes a ghost on every return. Fix: a module-scoped cache keyed by the entity, seeding `useState` initial value and starting `loading=false` when warm. Canonical: `CompetitionList.tsx:22` (`cachedProjectId`/`cachedCompetitions`), `:30` (`warmForProject`), `:40` (`useState(!warmForProject)`), `:57` (write-through). Precedent: `LifecyclePage.tsx` (`cachedDevClone`/`hasCachedData`).

## What a session does differently

When building any page that loads async data: reach for these four primitives instead of a `<Skeleton>` or a spinner. The net rule — **the delay lives on the placeholder, the placeholder ghosts only into genuine emptiness under permanent chrome, content reveals via the id-guarded cascade, and a remount paints from a module cache.** For tables, all four come free from `UnifiedTable` (see the sibling practice `promote:unifiedtable-cold-load-contract`).

observed.title: Make the handshake three legs, not two, to get mutual freshness
observed.statement: Two-leg handshakes prove key possession but not liveness: the initiator's first signature contains nothing the responder chose, so a recorded Hello replays forever. Add a third leg where the initiator signs the responder's nonce, and refuse to count the connection as established until it arrives (with a timeout).
